drought.title: Drought Classification
drought.description: Analyze satellite imagery to identify and classify drought conditions using vegetation and thermal indices.

howToUse.intro: Follow these steps to perform drought analysis:

steps.title: Draw ROI
steps.description: Use the polygon or rectangle tool on the map to define your region of interest.

steps.title: Set Date Range
steps.description: Select start and end dates to filter available Landsat 9 satellite images.

steps.title: Adjust Cloud Cover
steps.description: Use the slider to set maximum acceptable cloud coverage (lower values = clearer images).

steps.title: Browse & Select Image
steps.description: Use the image slider to preview available images and select the most suitable one.

steps.title: Extract Features
steps.description: Click 'Extract' to calculate vegetation indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDDI, EVI) and land surface temperature (LST) from the selected image.

steps.title: Run Prediction
steps.description: Click 'Predict' to apply the machine learning model and classify drought levels.

steps.title: Analyze Results
steps.description: View the classification results in the table and chart panels. Use index buttons to visualize different layers on the map.

features: Multi-spectral vegetation index calculation (NDVI, NDWI, NDDI, EVI)
Machine learning-based drought classification (Low, Medium, High)
Interactive map visualization with multiple layers
Data export functionality for further analysis

items.name: NDVI
items.description: Measures vegetation health. Higher values indicate healthier vegetation.

items.name: NDWI
items.description: Detects water content in vegetation and soil moisture levels.

items.name: NDDI
items.description: Combines NDVI and NDWI to assess drought conditions directly.

items.name: EVI
items.description: Improved vegetation index that reduces atmospheric interference.

items.name: LST
items.description: Surface temperature in Celsius, indicating thermal stress conditions.

tips: Select images during dry season for more accurate drought assessment.
Smaller ROI areas provide faster processing and more detailed results.
Compare multiple dates to track drought progression over time.

organic.title: Soil Classification
organic.description: Classify soil types based on nutrient composition and organic matter content using adaptive machine learning.

howToUse.intro: Follow these steps to perform soil classification:

steps.title: Draw ROI
steps.description: Use the polygon or rectangle tool on the map to define your area of interest.

steps.title: Set Date Range
steps.description: Select start and end dates to filter available satellite images for your analysis period.

steps.title: Adjust Cloud Cover
steps.description: Set the maximum cloud coverage threshold for image selection.

steps.title: Browse & Select Image
steps.description: Preview and select the most suitable satellite image for analysis.

steps.title: Extract Features
steps.description: Click 'Extract' to derive soil nutrient indicators (N, P, K, pH, SOM) from spectral data.

steps.title: Run Prediction
steps.description: Click 'Predict' to classify soil as Organic or Non-Organic using the adaptive ML model.

steps.title: Analyze Results
steps.description: Review classification results in the table and distribution chart. Toggle layers to visualize different soil parameters.

features: Adaptive machine learning with incremental PCA
Multi-parameter visualization (N, P, K, pH, SOM)
Interactive layer control for detailed analysis

items.name: N
items.description: Essential nutrient for plant growth. Higher values indicate nitrogen-rich soil.

items.name: P
items.description: Critical for root development and energy transfer in plants.

items.name: K
items.description: Important for water regulation and disease resistance in plants.

items.name: pH
items.description: Measures soil pH level. Optimal range varies by crop type.

items.name: SOM
items.description: Percentage of organic matter in soil. Higher values indicate better soil fertility.

tips: Organic soils typically show higher SOM values (>3%) and balanced NPK ratios.
Compare results across seasons to understand soil dynamics.
Use smaller ROIs for more accurate local soil classification.

dataviz.title: Fertilization Monitoring
dataviz.description: Visualize and analyze soil nutrient data from field measurements to monitor fertilization effectiveness over time.

howToUse.intro: Follow these steps to visualize fertilization data:

steps.title: Prepare Spreadsheet
steps.description: Create a Google Sheets document with columns: Timestamp, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Latitude, Longitude.

steps.title: Share Spreadsheet
steps.description: Set your Google Sheet to 'Anyone with the link can view' for the system to access it.

steps.title: Enter URL
steps.description: Paste the Google Sheets URL into the input field in the left panel.

steps.title: Collect Data
steps.description: Click 'Collect' to fetch and process your fertilization records.

steps.title: View Map Points
steps.description: Sampling locations appear as markers on the map. Click markers to view details.

steps.title: Analyze Trends
steps.description: Use the chart panel to visualize NPK trends over time and identify patterns.

steps.title: Export Data
steps.description: Click 'Export' to download processed data for further analysis.

features: Direct Google Sheets integration for easy data import
Automatic coordinate validation and data cleaning
Interactive data table with sorting and filtering
CSV export for external analysis tools
tips: Ensure all coordinates are in decimal degree format (e.g., -7.250, 110.400).
Remove any empty rows or invalid entries from your spreadsheet before importing.
Use consistent date/time formatting throughout your dataset.
Regular sampling intervals provide better trend analysis.
